title: Naturality and open restriction of the external evaluation transpose
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X,Y,P$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $a:P\to X$, $b:P\to Y$ scheme morphisms. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites in one module universe [def-weil-size-convention], in the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse image and derived tensor are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-kun-derived-tensor]. For any scheme $T$ and $G,M\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, set
$$\mathsf H_T(G,M)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_A(G,M))\in D(A),$$
using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the derived constant/sections adjunction [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]; write $\underline Q_T$ for constant realization [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. For every $Q\in D(A)$ there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q,\mathsf H_T(G,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,A)}(\underline Q_T\otimes_A^LG,M).$$
It sends the identity of $\mathsf H_T(G,M)$ to evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}$.

For arbitrary $E,K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $H,L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $C=\mathsf H_X(E,K)$, $D=\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$, $G=a^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H$ and $F=a^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}L$. The transpose of
$$\underline{C\otimes_A^LD}_P\otimes_A^LG\xrightarrow{\chi}(a^{-1}\underline C_X\otimes_A^La^{-1}E)\otimes_A^L(b^{-1}\underline D_Y\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H)\xrightarrow{a^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{E,K}\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{H,L}}F$$
is a well-defined morphism $\beta_{E,H}:C\otimes_A^LD\to\mathsf H_P(G,F)$. Here $\chi$ uses the canonical constant-pullback and strong monoidal comparisons and the symmetry interchanging $\underline D$ with $a^{-1}E$, whose cochain sign is $(-1)^{|z||e|}$. The morphisms $\beta$ are contravariantly natural in $E,H$ and covariantly natural in $K,L$. For an open immersion $j:X'\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], put $P'=P\times_X X'$, $k:P'\to P$, $a':P'\to X'$ and $b'=bk$. Restriction of global derived morphisms induces maps on each $\mathsf H$; the square from $\beta_{E,H}$ to $\beta_{j^{-1}E,H}$ with these restriction maps commutes under $k^{-1}G\cong a'^{-1}j^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb'^{-1}H$ and $k^{-1}F\cong a'^{-1}j^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb'^{-1}L$. The analogous assertion holds for restriction of $Y$. No boundedness or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The bounded-domain four-variable naturality specialization is already proved by GenericExternal.naturality, with exactly the canonical constant/sections adjunctions, pullback tensor constraints and constant comparisons. The unrestricted combined theorem retains all of its original clauses and its source argument below.

Put $L_TQ=\underline Q_T$, $R_T=R\Gamma(T,-)$ and $I_T(G,M)=R\mathcal Hom_A(G,M)$. The constant/sections adjunction of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] and the closed adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], applied on the small ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_T)$, give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,R_TI_T(G,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_TQ,I_T(G,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_TQ\otimes_A^LG,M).$$
All three objects are arbitrary unbounded objects, as allowed in both cited statements. If $\varepsilon$ is the constant/sections counit and $e$ the internal tensor-Hom counit, define $\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}=e_{G,M}\circ(\varepsilon_{I_T(G,M)}\otimes1_G)$. The explicit counit formula in the closed-adjunction statement shows that the displayed bijection sends $f:Q\to\mathsf H_T(G,M)$ to $\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}\circ(L_Tf\otimes1_G)$. In particular the identity has the required image. Denote the inverse bijection by $\operatorname{tr}_T$.

proof.text:
For $u:G'\to G$ and $v:M\to M'$, let $h=\mathsf H_T(u,v):\mathsf H_T(G,M)\to\mathsf H_T(G',M')$. Naturality of the two bijections in step 1 gives the equality
$$\mathrm{ev}_{G',M'}\circ(L_Th\otimes1_{G'})=v\circ\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}\circ(1\otimes u).$$
Indeed both sides are the untranspose of $h$, the right side by naturality in $G,M$, the left side by naturality in $Q$. Thus this equation follows from the stated naturality of the closed adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and of $L_T\dashv R_T$ [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], without an additional evaluation lemma.

proof.text:
Construct $\chi$ by first replacing $L_P(C\otimes_A^LD)$ with $L_PC\otimes_A^LL_PD$, replacing these constants by $a^{-1}L_XC$ and $b^{-1}L_YD$, then reassociating and interchanging the middle two factors $b^{-1}L_YD$ and $a^{-1}E$. Constant pullback is exactly [def-pur-derived-constant-pullback-comparison]. Scheme inverse image is exact module pullback by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; its derived tensor comparison and signed coherence are therefore supplied by [lem-pur-exact-pullback-signed-comparison]. The same result applies to constant realization, the exact module inverse image from the one-point site with ring $A$, as identified in [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. The signed symmetric monoidal structure is [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Thus $\chi$ is a natural isomorphism, with middle interchange $z\otimes e\mapsto(-1)^{|z||e|}e\otimes z$. Put
$$B=(a^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{E,K}\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{H,L})\circ\chi.$$
It has source $L_P(C\otimes_A^LD)\otimes_A^LG$ and target $F$. Define $\beta=\operatorname{tr}_P(B)$ using step 1. Every map is a map of the specified derived categories, so this definition needs no choice of resolutions or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text:
Take $u:E'\to E$, $v:H'\to H$, $s:K\to K'$, $t:L\to L'$. Write $c=\mathsf H_X(u,s):C\to C'$, $d=\mathsf H_Y(v,t):D\to D'$, $g=a^{-1}u\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}v:G'\to G$, and $f=a^{-1}s\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}t:F\to F'$. Tensoring the two evaluation equations of step 2 and using naturality of every factor of $\chi$ gives
$$B'\circ(L_P(c\otimes_A^Ld)\otimes1_{G'})=f\circ B\circ(1\otimes g).$$
Here naturality of the signed interchange is the naturality assertion of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], and the pullback tensor comparisons are natural by [lem-pur-exact-pullback-signed-comparison]. By the formula for untransposition in step 1, these are the untransposes of $\beta'\circ(c\otimes_A^Ld)$ and $\mathsf H_P(g,f)\circ\beta$. Injectivity of that bijection proves their equality. Setting three of $u,v,s,t$ to identities proves naturality separately in each of the four variables.

proof.text:
For an open $j:T'\hookrightarrow T$, identify the small etale site of $T'$ with the slice of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ at $T'\to T$: an object is precisely an etale $V\to T$ equipped with a map $V\to T'$ over $T$, and coverings are the same. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), applied to the etale morphism $j$, the scheme inverse image $j^{-1}$ is identified with this restriction by a natural isomorphism $\rho$, termwise on complexes; being natural, $\rho$ respects the $A$-actions, and both tensor comparisons send a local $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$, so they agree under $\rho$. Write $j^*$ for this restriction. For $Z\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the derived-sections restriction $s_Z:R_TZ\to R_{T'}j^*Z$ is the $L_{T'}\dashv R_{T'}$ adjunct of
$$L_{T'}R_TZ\cong j^*L_TR_TZ\xrightarrow{j^*\varepsilon_Z}j^*Z.$$
This is the usual restriction (clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]: under $\rho$ the unit of $j^{-1}\dashv j_*$ is restriction of sections): under the constants/sections adjunction it sends a constant-source morphism to its pullback. The canonical constant comparison is [def-pur-derived-constant-pullback-comparison]. The counit formula for the adjunction [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] gives, with that comparison understood,
$$\varepsilon_{j^*Z}\circ L_{T'}s_Z=j^*\varepsilon_Z.$$
This equation is simply the inverse Hom-bijection applied to its defining adjunct, so no invertibility of the sections restriction is asserted.

proof.text:
Let $\eta:j^*I_T(G,M)\cong I_{T'}(j^*G,j^*M)$ be the canonical restriction comparison. The node [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] states both its existence for arbitrary unbounded objects and its compatibility with the internal evaluation counit. Define the restriction on global derived Hom by
$$r_j=R_{T'}(\eta)\circ s_{I_T(G,M)}.$$
This is restriction of global derived morphisms, since $s$ restricts sections and $\eta$ restricts internal Hom. Naturality of the constant/sections counit, then step 5, gives
$$\varepsilon_{I_{T'}(j^*G,j^*M)}\circ L_{T'}r_j=\eta\circ j^*\varepsilon_{I_T(G,M)}.$$
Insert this into the formula for global evaluation in step 1 and use the internal evaluation equation of the cited slice node. With the canonical tensor and constant comparisons suppressed, the result is
$$\mathrm{ev}_{j^*G,j^*M}\circ(L_{T'}r_j\otimes1_{j^*G})=j^*\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}.$$
Consequently, for any $w:Q\to\mathsf H_T(G,M)$, the untranspose of $r_jw$ is $j^*$ of the untranspose of $w$. This follows by composing the displayed equality with $L_{T'}w\otimes1$.

proof.text: The constant-pullback identifications used here respect composition. In fact [lem-weil-pbc-constant-pullback-composition-coherence] states the equality before deriving, for every abelian group. Apply it to each underlying abelian group $Q^n$ of a complex of $A$-modules. All comparison maps respect the $A$-action because they are induced by constant sections; the equality commutes with the differentials by naturality. Localizing therefore gives the same equality for $Q\in D(A)$, using the termwise construction in [def-pur-derived-constant-pullback-comparison]. In particular the two constant identifications for $k^{-1}a^{-1}$ and $a'^{-1}j^{-1}$ coincide when $ak=ja'$; the analogous assertion holds for $b'=bk$.

proof.text: For the square in the statement, identify $k^{-1}a^{-1}$ with $a'^{-1}j^{-1}$ and $k^{-1}b^{-1}$ with $b'^{-1}$. The node [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] gives the tensor compatibility of these canonical composition comparisons. The associator and symmetry equations of [lem-pur-exact-pullback-signed-comparison] show that $k^{-1}$ preserves the reassociation and middle interchange used in $\chi$. Together with the constants equality of step 7 these give equality of $k^{-1}\chi$ with the corresponding $\chi'$ after the canonical identifications of all four input factors. More explicitly, for the constants use the cochain composition equation of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] for the structural ringed-site maps to the one-point site. On flat-term K-flat representatives its equality localizes to the desired equality, by the unique representative formula of [lem-pur-exact-pullback-signed-comparison]; these exact pullbacks preserve such representatives. For the two geometric inverse images use [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] for $(a,k)$ and $(j,a')$, and for $(b,k)$. The only nontrivial permutation is still interchange of the $D$ and $a^{-1}E$ factors, preserved by the cited symmetry equation. Thus every factor of the two composites agrees, not just their underlying objects.

proof.text:
The morphism $k:P\times_XX'\to P$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], applied to the open immersion $j$ and the arbitrary morphism $a$; likewise for the open pullback over $Y$. Put $C'=\mathsf H_{X'}(j^{-1}E,j^{-1}K)$ and let $r_X:C\to C'$ and $r_P:\mathsf H_P(G,F)\to\mathsf H_{P'}(k^{-1}G,k^{-1}F)$ be the restrictions of step 6. Write $B'$ for the external untransposed evaluation constructed on $(X',Y,P')$. Applying the evaluation equation of step 6 on $X$ yields
$$a'^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{j^{-1}E,j^{-1}K}\circ(a'^{-1}L_{X'}r_X\otimes1)=k^{-1}a^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{E,K}.$$
The second evaluation is unchanged, with $b'^{-1}=k^{-1}b^{-1}$. Tensor these equalities and insert the $\chi$ equality of step 8. They give
$$B'\circ(L_{P'}(r_X\otimes_A^L1_D)\otimes1_{k^{-1}G})=k^{-1}B.$$
By step 6 on $P$, the right side is the untranspose of $r_P\beta$. By step 1 the left side is the untranspose of $\beta'\circ(r_X\otimes_A^L1_D)$. Injectivity proves the required restriction square. For an open $j_Y:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$, put $P''=P\times_YY'$, restrict the second evaluation instead, and use the identical equality with $1_C\otimes r_Y$ in place of $r_X\otimes1_D$. The first evaluation is then unchanged and the same middle interchange is preserved by step 8, so its square also commutes. All cited adjunctions and comparisons hold on unbounded objects; no flatness or boundedness hypothesis was introduced.
